Positive decimal times use explicit rounding; a rounded zero clamps to one simulation step as upstream Timer does. Exact mode rejects fractional steps; nonpositive inputs reject before rounding. C# supports decimal/ulong rather than arbitrary Fraction/float numeric protocols and omits mutable class-wide rounding defaults and deprecated units spelling. Runtime.Steps intentionally remains a strict conversion helper.

Stable read-only callback and rejection of ReadOnly/ReadWrite reentry are tested. C# trigger identity is not the Python singleton identity; this classification covers phase semantics.
Runtime flushes scheduled deposits before queued ReadWrite continuations and rejects entry from ReadOnly. Callback object identity is not preserved.
Uses next-time callback rather than a delta-cycle yield. Test schedules a future timer and requires time advance; no promise to advance absent future simulator events.

reviews.reason: ValueChange accepts HdlObject scalar value families, including RealSignal, StringSignal and IntegerSignal, while preserving the Signal overload. Scopes and aggregates reject before callback allocation. Real callbacks pass on Icarus and NVC; fixed strings pass on NVC, including same-value writes, fanout, cancellation, reuse and cleanup. Python cached trigger identity is not preserved; dynamic-string callback and broader backend coverage are not established.
Deprecated public Edge alias is omitted; use Triggers.ValueChange for supported scalar value objects.

LastSimulatorCallback exposes actual callback kind, time and original native Trigger identity; runtime-owned callbacks have null Trigger. Tests distinguish Timer/NextStep/synchronization/value-change, internal deadlines, wrapper origin and unchanged snapshots after managed waits or rejected/cancelled registration. Unlike Python, this includes internal callbacks and is null before any actual callback rather than fabricating a startup Timer. Runtime-wide rather than task-local.
TryPut returns false for occupied or reserved capacity instead of raising QueueFull; no Python exception inheritance is provided.
TryGet returns false and default(T) when no unreserved item exists; a true result may contain null. No QueueEmpty exception type.
SimQueueBase shares built-in coordination but intentionally does not expose external storage hooks; private protected construction protects transactional permit accounting.
Count reports physical FIFO occupancy, including values reserved for a pending consumer. Tested during immediate operations and reserved handoffs.
Capacity is immutable and strictly positive, default int.MaxValue; nonpositive sizes do not mean unbounded as in Python.
IsEmpty describes physical occupancy, not whether another caller may consume a reserved item. Handoff tests distinguish these states.
IsFull reports Count == Capacity with positive finite capacity; there is no Python nonpositive-unbounded mode. A free physical slot may be reserved.
Put uses FIFO reserved slots and cancellable semaphore acquisition rather than wake-and-recheck occupancy. Tests cover blocked producers, cancellation before handoff cleanup and pre-cancelled tokens.
TryPut is immediate and boolean; it refuses to steal slots reserved for queued producers even if the physical queue is not full.

Get transfers oldest FIFO items using reserved item permits. Cancellation returns granted-but-unconsumed permits to surviving waiters; unlike Python occupancy loops, newcomers cannot steal a reservation.
TryGet returns boolean/out value and refuses to steal reserved items even if Count is positive; tests verify null payloads and default on failure.

SimQueue<T> provides FIFO payload ordering and bounded waiting with positive-capacity, explicit cancellation and reservation semantics. Those differences are documented and tested rather than claimed exact Python behavior.
SimPriorityQueue consumes IComparer<T>/Comparer<T>.Default instead of Python rich comparison; payload and null ordering follow the selected comparer.

SimPriorityQueue implements smallest-first bounded waits and immediate operations. Stable equal priorities, transactional comparer failures and reserved waiters are explicit differences from Python heap/wake-and-recheck semantics.
SimLifoQueue implements newest-first storage with shared cancellation and reserved FIFO waiter permits; pinned immediate ordering and occupancy are compared automatically.

CountOf counts values using EqualityComparer<T>.Default or a custom comparer rather than Python equality.
ValueArray<T> indexer and transactional SetSlice provide fixed-size mutation; external abstract storage hooks are unsupported.

ValueArray<T> copies input, indexes by HDL bounds and supports reindexing, slicing and transactional slice assignment. Explicit constructor bounds, null slices, reference equality and lack of Python protocols are documented differences.
ValueArray.Range gets/sets same-size declared bounds without reordering stored values; failed length validation preserves original bounds.

HdlRange.Ascending uses a boolean rather than a string enum; both declared directions and null ranges are retained.
HdlRange has inclusive directed bounds, null ranges, membership and iteration. Int32 bounds, structural equality, nonnegative positions and explicit construction differ from Python protocols.
Python range conversion is not exposed; System.Range cannot represent descending/negative HDL ranges. Construct HdlRange explicitly.
HdlRange implements IEnumerable<int> instead of returning a Python range or incompatible half-open System.Range.
HdlRange.Left retains the declared left bound, including null ranges, within Int32 limits.
HdlRange.Ascending retains declared direction as a boolean instead of a string.
HdlRange.Right retains the inclusive right bound, including null ranges, within Int32 limits.
HdlRange.Offset maps an HDL index to its position; missing indices throw IndexOutOfRangeException. Optional Python positional search windows and arbitrary-size offsets are not exposed.

Pinned capture calls synchronously and wraps any Python BaseException with traceback-frame stripping. C# StartJob schedules the body and captures .NET exceptions in TaskCompletionSource; it is not a synchronous capture API and does not rewrite Python tracebacks. Deferred execution and test supervision are retained intentionally.

The pinned completed-outcome abstraction has Value/Error subclasses. C# uses Task/Task<T> completion state and SimJob wrappers; no public Outcome class or Python outcome protocol is provided. Pending and cancelled tasks are separate .NET states, not additional Python Outcome variants.

Upstream abstract get is implemented by completed value/error wrappers. C# typed Result explicitly rejects unfinished jobs instead of blocking the simulator, and awaits propagate completion/failure/cancellation. This is a stateful job contract rather than a callable completed Outcome interface.

reviews.reason: A successful typed job retains its value in Task<T>, exposed by await and completed Result. This covers value propagation, not Python wrapper construction, representation, identity or direct value-field mutation.

Pinned Value.get immediately returns its stored object. C# completed Result returns the same typed value, while incomplete access fails; the result is immutable through this API. The typed job regression checks value survives awaiting and subsequent Result reads.

Pinned Error stores a Python BaseException. C# faults Task<T> and exposes AggregateException through Task.Exception while await/GetAwaiter.GetResult rethrows the underlying .NET exception. Python traceback manipulation and BaseException taxonomy are outside this mapping.

Pinned Error.get raises its stored exception. C# GetAwaiter.GetResult on a faulted job throws the original FormatException; existing completion/introspection regressions check the original error and managed stack. Exception-class identity across Python and .NET is not claimed.

Pinned wait exposes FIRST_COMPLETED/FIRST_EXCEPTION/ALL_COMPLETED with waiter Tasks and an optional first index, owning raw awaitables while borrowing existing Tasks. SharpTestBench intentionally exposes high-level Gather/Select and non-owning First/Combine instead of this low-level policy/result tuple. Heterogeneous Python overloads are one contract review, not separate engineered features. This mapping does not establish the absent public wait API or upstream cancellation internals.
